A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Electrostatic Field Matching work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved from v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix D.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll transport, colored MNIST 3-to-2 translation, and digit-2 generation experiments, illustrated in Figures 5–10.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D report original transport and image-generation results, including full MNIST, CIFAR-10, sensitivity experiments, and additional baseline outputs.

M1.justification: The stated training objective changes from matching E to matching E/||E||, and the interpolation and noise-sampling formulas are revised. The ideal transport is redefined through flux-weighted stochastic forward/backward and stopping choices. V2 explicitly distinguishes this construction from its practical forward-only sampler, which stops at the first target-plane crossing.

E1.justification: V2 expands generation from colored digit 2 to all MNIST digits and adds CIFAR-10 natural images. Appendix C.2 also adds transport to a separated two-Gaussian target. Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll transport and colored 3-to-2 translation remain.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 23 adds Cycle-GAN, DDIB, and DSBM outputs for the retained colored MNIST translation task, substantially expanding comparison beyond v1's Flow Matching baseline. PFGM remains the image-generation comparator.

E3.justification: Toy inference is now specified through the z-parameterized Algorithm 2 rather than v1's raw-field Euler update in Eq. (40). Added protocols vary CIFAR-10 plate distance over 50, 500, and 5000 and compare interpolation-based training points with a uniform cube mesh. Existing Table 1 parameter values and image RK45, Adam, and EMA settings remain unchanged; rerunning retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Swiss-roll distance example, v2 adds CIFAR-10 distance sensitivity, a Gaussian-to-two-Gaussians boundary-crossing failure case, and an interpolation-versus-cube-mesh training-volume comparison (Appendix C, Figures 19, 20, and 22). These substantially expand evidence about sensitivity and failure mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's references to significant visual differences do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: V1's digit-2 generation panels are replaced by full-MNIST samples, and v2 adds CIFAR-10 samples and three translation-baseline outputs. New findings include degraded CIFAR-10 generation at L=5000 and similar Swiss-roll recovery with two training-volume constructions. Retained Swiss-roll and translation comparison panels are unchanged; the expanded results do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 now explicitly assumes compact support and concerns the stochastic transport map. Appendix B replaces v1's half-charge-flux argument with field-jump, branching, and termination lemmas plus flux accounting across multiple plane crossings. This substantially revises the definitions and proof, although the replacement proof introduces an unexplained Φ0 in Eq. (56).

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central contribution: an electrostatics-based method for both noise-to-data and data-to-data transport, with theoretical justification and toy/image demonstrations. The expanded evidence and revised formal construction do not change this overarching contribution claim.

C2.justification: V1 discusses dimensionality, plate distance, and training-volume selection. V2 additionally explains that first-crossing termination can distort the target distribution and that omitting backward trajectories can leave target support uncovered, particularly with shifted distributions. Section 5 and Appendix C make the gap between theoretical transport and practical implementation explicit.

D1.justification: V2 adds sampling pseudocode, CIFAR-10 hyperparameters including L=500 and sigma=0.05, and code-source links for Cycle-GAN, DDIB, and DSBM. Existing optimizer, solver tolerances, EMA, GPU, and training-time disclosures are retained in the relocated experimental-details appendix.

R1.justification: References add Peluchetti (2023), Su et al. (2023), and De Bortoli et al. (2024), while removing the variational-diffusion and adversarial Schrödinger-bridge works cited in v1. Appendix C.4 adds a specific contrast with Flow Matching's interpolation-dependent loss. The overall electrostatic/PFGM positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reworks the electrostatics and transport exposition, restructures the main proof into auxiliary lemmas and numbered steps, and expands explanations throughout the retained material. An extended limitations appendix is inserted, with experimental details moved from Appendix C to D. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 adds stochastic-map and proof diagrams, CIFAR-10 panels, sensitivity/failure illustrations, and additional baseline panels. MNIST generation panels are replaced, the original multipart flux illustration is simplified, and Table 1 gains a CIFAR-10 row. Retained figures are largely renumbered, but the new and revised displays substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important omission in v1: how field-line direction and repeated plane crossings affect distribution transfer. Its explicit stochastic construction, revised proof, and candid explanation of the practical approximation substantially improve scientific precision. Targeted failure and sensitivity experiments strengthen that explanation. Results remain qualitative, and the revised proof has notation problems such as unexplained Φ0 in Eq. (56), but the clearer theoretical scope and experimentally illustrated limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
